title: How to organize the guest nightstand | Guest Bedroom
description:
The handful of things a guest needs in the middle of the night without knocking on your door.

This is the Guest Nightstand in the Guest Bedroom. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A lamp whose switch you can find by feel in the dark, one charging cable per common connector plugged in and reaching the pillow, a coaster, a box of tissues at least half full, and a drawer that is genuinely empty apart from a card with the wifi name and password.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Open the drawer and take out what has been hiding in a room nobody uses: dead batteries, a clock radio that lost its time when the power blipped, three paperbacks nobody chose, cough drops fused into their tin.
Straighten: Set the lamp on the side a right hand reaches first from the pillow, run the charger head over the top edge of the nightstand so it hangs where a hand lands, and stand the tissue box upright rather than laying it in the drawer.
Shine: Wipe the lamp base and the inner rim of the shade, vacuum the drawer out rather than wiping it, and clean the water ring the last guest left because they could not find the coaster.
Safety: The water glass, the lamp cord and the outlet all meet in one square foot here, so run the cord behind the nightstand rather than across the top, and keep the glass on the far side from the lamp.
Standardize: Tape a small card inside the drawer with the wifi name and password, where the bathroom is, and which way the shower tap turns.
Sustain: The night before an arrival, switch the lamp on and plug your own phone into each cable while you make the bed, so a dead bulb or a failed cable is found by you rather than by them at two in the morning.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Lamp, two proven cables, tissues, coaster, wifi card.
